passage:
A museum displayed a small clay animal made by a child long ago. It was uneven, with one leg shorter than the others.
Students were surprised that such an ordinary object was in a museum. The guide said ancient children played, learned, and made imperfect things too.
The toy made the past feel less distant. People long ago were not only builders of temples or fighters in wars. They were also children making animals from clay.
The object was not famous, but it was human.
Sometimes the smallest historical items create the strongest connection because they show daily life rather than power.
